Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Mumbai techie looking for extra income through WFH job loses Rs 90.8L, makes 525 UPI transfers to fraudsters over 3 years, even uses father's pension before threats of arrest, morphed photos push her
Article Text:
A Bhandup woman fell victim to a work-from-home data-entry scam, losing Rs 90.8 lakh. (AI image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: East Cyber police registered an FIR on Nov 11 against five unidentified people for allegedly cheating a 31-year-old Bhandup woman of Rs 90.8 lakh in a work-from-home data-entry scam and threatening her with arrest and morphed photographs.The woman, employed by an AI-based IT solutions company in Thane, had responded to a data-entry job advertisement on Instagram on Sept 28, 2023, to earn additional income. The accused allegedly obtained her documents and photographs before demanding payments towards registration, forms, GST, CGST and company policy.Police said she made 525 UPI transfers to various bank accounts between 2023 and 2026. After exhausting her savings, she allegedly transferred her father's pension to her account to meet the demands. Her father retired from the ST Department in 2015, and the family was supported by his pension and her salary.According to the complaint, WhatsApp users identifying themselves as Khushbu Khan, Nashrat Anjum and Wasim Khan allegedly conspired with other mobile users and beneficiary account holders. They repeatedly sent her scanners and UPI details for payments.The accused allegedly threatened to file false police complaints against the woman and her family and have them arrested if she stopped paying.They also threatened to circulate morphed objectionable images using her photograph and defame her on social media.Unable to bear the trauma, the woman informed her father and approached cyber police. She also lodged four online complaints through the 1930 cybercrime helpline. Police have asked banks to freeze the recipient accounts.State Cyber Cell data showed victims lost Rs 303.6 crore between 2021 and 2025, of which Rs 12.1 crore was recovered. Mumbai accounted for 54% of Maharashtra's 2,594 job fraud or work-from-home scam cases during the period. Of 333 solved cases statewide, 274 were in Mumbai.Cyber expert Ritesh Bhatia has advised citizens tnot to fall prey to work-from-home messages as almost all of them are scams.
Article Summary: A 31-year-old Bhandup woman fell victim to a work-from-home scam, losing Rs 90.8 lakh. The woman responded to a data-entry job advertisement on Instagram on Sept 28, 2023. The accused allegedly obtained her documents and photographs before demanding payments.

Article Title: Gurgaon woman pays Rs 4,811 for dinner, restaurant refuses to remove Rs 401 service charge despite objection; consumer commission says mandatory service charge violates CCPA rules, orders refund and R
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





GURGAON: A dinner outing with friends in Gurgaon ended in a consumer dispute after a woman was charged an additional 10% service fee despite asking the restaurant to remove it. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the restaurant to pay her Rs 31,000, including compensation for mental harassment and litigation expenses. It has also ordered a refund of the Rs 401 service charge.The dispute dates back to May 16, 2026, when the woman visited the restaurant with her friends for dinner. She alleged that the bill included a service charge of Rs 401, equivalent to 10% of the amount. She objected to the additional charge and asked the restaurant to remove it. However, the establishment allegedly refused, leaving her with no option but to pay the entire bill of Rs 4,811, including the disputed fee.The woman later approached the consumer commission, arguing that the restaurant had violated the Central Consumer Protection Authority's (CCPA) guidelines on service charges. The restaurant did not appear before the commission despite being given an opportunity to respond. The proceedings were therefore conducted ex parte.In its order, the commission referred to the CCPA's guidelines issued on July 4, 2022, which prohibit hotels and restaurants from automatically adding a service charge to bills.The guidelines state that establishments cannot collect such charges by default or under another name. They also make clear that payment of a service charge must remain voluntary, with consumers free to decide whether they want to pay it.The commission said the restaurant had disregarded these provisions by refusing to remove the charge despite the customer's objection. It held the establishment guilty of deficiency in service and adopting an unfair trade practice, observing that its actions amounted to a blatant violation of the CCPA guidelines. Apart from ordering the restaurant to return the Rs 401 collected as service charge, the commission awarded the woman Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and financial loss. It also directed the restaurant to pay Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses, taking the total amount payable to Rs 31,401, including the refund.
Article Summary: A woman was charged an additional 10% service fee despite asking the restaurant to remove it. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has ordered the establishment to pay her Rs 31,000. The commission awarded the woman Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and financial loss.

Article Title: Bengaluru woman deposits Rs 4L in FD with cooperative society, gets back Rs 3L after maturity but is made to wait for remaining amount, consumer commission orders society to pay Rs 1.12L with 12% inte
Article Text:
Society had returned Rs 3 lakh of her Rs 4 lakh deposits but failed to pay balance despite repeated requests; consumer commission awards Rs 30,000 compensation and legal costs (AI image)​

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





BENGALURU: The Bengaluru Urban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Sree Thyagarajanagara Credit Co-operative Society to refund Rs 1,12,304 to a woman towards her outstanding fixed deposit amount, along with 12% annual interest from February 4, 2023, until realisation.The commission also ordered the society to pay Rs 20,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. It has been given 45 days to comply with the order.The complaint was filed by K P Vanajakshi, a resident of Banashankari II Stage, who had deposited a total of Rs 4 lakh in five fixed deposit accounts with the cooperative society.According to the complaint, Vanajakshi became a member of the society on November 19, 2016, and purchased 50 shares of Rs 100 each. Her husband was also a member of the society.She had deposited Rs 50,000 each in two fixed deposit accounts and Rs 1 lakh each in three other accounts, taking the total investment to Rs 4 lakh.After the deposits matured, the society transferred the amounts to her savings bank account instead of directly paying her. Despite repeated requests for repayment along with the agreed interest, the society paid only Rs 1 lakh on February 4, 2023, and another Rs 2 lakh on April 3, 2024.The remaining amount was not paid. Vanajakshi's husband also made several representations to the society and approached the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies in Bengaluru on September 30, 2024.The complainant subsequently sent another representation through registered post on May 28, 2025, seeking withdrawal of the outstanding amount, but the society failed to comply.In its defence, the society admitted that Vanajakshi had deposited Rs 4 lakh in five fixed deposit accounts and that it had repaid Rs 3 lakh. It also acknowledged that Rs 1,12,304, including the applicable interest, remained payable.However, the society cited a financial crisis and shortage of funds, claiming that several members who had borrowed money from it had defaulted on loan repayments. It said the defaults had affected its financial stability and left it unable to return the remaining deposit amount.The society also argued that the complainant had earlier approached the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies over the same issue.After examining the documents and submissions, the commission observed that the society had admitted both the fixed deposits and its liability to repay the outstanding amount. It noted that the society had accepted the deposits and was obligated to honour the terms and conditions after their maturity.The commission held that the society's failure to repay the entire matured deposit amount, despite making partial payments and acknowledging the outstanding liability, amounted to deficiency in service.It observed that the society could not escape its responsibility to return the depositor's money by citing its own financial difficulties arising from loan defaults by other members.Allowing the complaint in part, the commission directed the society to pay Rs 1,12,304 with 12% annual interest from February 4, 2023, until realisation, along with Rs 20,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation costs.The order was passed on October 17, 2026, by commission president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani.
Article Summary: K P Vanajakshi had deposited Rs 4 lakh in five fixed deposit accounts with the cooperative society. Society had returned Rs 3 lakh of the deposits but failed to pay balance despite repeated requests. Sree Thyagarajanagara Credit Co- operative Society has been ordered to refund Rs 1,12,304.

Article Title: Short circuit triggers fire at Solapur textile factory, owner files Rs 87.33L claim, United India rejects it citing unauthorised construction; consumer commission orders insurer to pay Rs 87.33L after
Article Text:
Abhishek Dhanresha, owner of Mateshri Textiles, faced an insurance claim repudiation from United India Insurance after a factory fire (AI image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: Abhishek Dhanresha was the proprietor of Mateshri Textiles which manufactured towels and napkins at Solapur.The unit was insured by United India Insurance under three policies - one for the factory building, the second for plant and machinery, and the third for the stock of finished and semi-finished goods, and raw materials.The total coverage under all the three policies amounted to Rs.91,50,000/. Prior to issuing the policies, the insurer had conducted a thorough inspection of the factory premises along with photographic documentation.On July 21, 2017 an electrical short circuit caused an accidental fire in the factory premises. This was immediately communicated to the police, fire department, electrical inspector, and the insurer. Later, a comprehensive claim for Rs.87,33,324/ was lodged.The insurer appointed a surveyor to assess the loss. Over a year later, the insurer sent a letter dated July 16, 2018 intimating that the claim was repudiated on the ground that there was illegal construction and unauthorized electric connection on the ground and second floors.Besides, the absence of fire extinguishing appliances was construed as negligence and a breach of the terms of the policy.The insured filed a complaint before the Maharashtra State Commission challenging the repudiation.The State Commission observed that the crux of the dispute was the unauthorized construction, unauthorized electricity connection, and absence of fire-fighting appliances.However, it noted that the insurer had had inspected the premises and then issued the policy with open eyes without raising any objection in respect of the alleged lapses and breaches.Hence the Commission concluded that the insurer could not be allowed to subsequently raise objections to avoid settlement of the claim and defeat the objective of taking insurance coverage.
Article Summary: Abhishek Dhanresha was the proprietor of Mateshri Textiles which manufactured towels and napkins at Solapur. The unit was insured by United India Insurance under three policies. On July 21, 2017 an electrical short circuit caused an accidental fire in the factory premises.

Article Title: Brexit rethink? UK PM Burnham admits Britain lost more than it gained
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to acknowledge that Britain has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union. He argue that the country's post-Brexit arrangement created economic difficulties and failed to fulfil key promises made during the 2016 referendum.According to the BBC, Burnham will make the remarks at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday, ahead of a UK-EU summit scheduled for Friday.He is expected to compare Britain's Brexit settlement to the story of "The Emperor's New Clothes", arguing that political leaders have been unwilling to acknowledge its shortcomings."It's like the emperor's new clothes, where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on," he is expected to say."The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained," Burnham will add.He will also describe Brexit as "needlessly hard", saying it created barriers for businesses while failing to deliver on the promise to "take back control", BBC reported.Burnham's criticism is directed at the terms under which Britain left the EU rather than the decision to leave the bloc itself.He has argued that the previous government's approach resulted in a harder Brexit, creating additional barriers for businesses and limiting the benefits of Britain's departure.He is expected to set three tests for any new agreement with Brussels. According to the BBC, the first is that any deal must remain consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto, which ruled out rejoining the EU's single market and customs union or restoring freedom of movement.The second is the "Makerfield test", which requires any agreement to bring tangible improvements to people's everyday lives. The third is that the new arrangement must improve the original Brexit deal and come closer to what people believed they were voting for in 2016.Britain voted to leave the European Union in a referendum held on June 23, 2016. The Leave campaign secured 51.9 per cent of the vote, while 48.1 per cent voted to remain in the bloc.The referendum was held after then prime minister David Cameron promised a public vote on EU membership ahead of the 2015 general election. Cameron had campaigned for Britain to remain in the bloc but announced his resignation after the Leave campaign won.Britain formally left the EU on January 31, 2020, after the government triggered Article 50 in March 2017. However, the transition period continued until December 31, 2020, when Britain also left the EU single market and customs union.The departure brought an end to frictionless trade arrangements and introduced additional customs procedures, paperwork and regulatory checks on goods moving between Britain and the EU. These changes increased costs and administrative requirements for businesses trading with the bloc.
Article Summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham set to acknowledge that Britain has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union. He will argue that the country's post-Brexit arrangement created economic difficulties and failed to fulfil key promises made during the 2016 referendum.

Article Title: India’s 5th-gen stealth AMCA aircraft: Bids of 3 consortiums submitted, evaluation under way
Article Text:
The AMCA is likely to be powered by twin F414 engines if the proposed deal between defence PSU Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd and US-based GE for their joint production in India materialises

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a big step towards developing India’s fifth-generation stealth fighter aircraft, three Indian contenders have submitted bids to a high-level review committee constituted by the defence ministry for prototype development for the Rs 15,000-crore Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft programme with their evaluation process now on.Industry sources confirmed to TOI that the three contenders — L&T-led consortium of BEL and Dynamatic, Tata Advanced Systems Ltd (TASL), and Bharat Forge-led consortium of BEML Ltd and Data Patterns — submitted their individual bids on Oct 30, the deadline for submission. Of the three, only TASL is the solitary bidder.“The bids were opened on Nov 1 to select a development-cum-production partner (DCPP) for developing five AMCA prototypes (designed by DRDO laboratory Aeronautical Development Agency),” the sources told TOI. The Bengaluru-based ADA, which conceived the project, will oversee the manufacturing of five twin-engine AMCA prototypes.The AMCA is likely to be powered by twin F414 engines if the proposed deal between defence PSU Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd and US-based GE for their joint production in India materialises. ADA requires 15 F414 engines for five flying prototypes for the AMCA project.The five prototypes are expected to undertake 1,800 test sorties in a period of seven years to validate the fighter’s flight-control systems, stealth characteristics, sensors, radar, weapons integration and propulsion performance.AMCA, once ready, will help the Indian Air Force acquire the fifth-generation fighter jet at a time. However, the first batch of the AMCA is expected to be ready around 2034 or 2035. AMCA is also meant to plug the shortfall in the IAF fighter squadrons, which have already come down to an alarming 29 against a sanctioned strength of 42.5. The deadline was earlier extended from Aug 27 to Oct 30 after bidders sought more time to complete formalities for the complex stealth aircraft programme.The aircraft’s stealth features include internal weapons bays, supercruise capability, advanced AI-driven avionics and next-generation sensor fusion.China is already operating two primary fifth-generation stealth fighter jets, Chengdu J-20 and the Shenyang J-35, and Pakistan is also planning to buy 40 Chinese J-35 stealth aircraft.
Article Summary: Three Indian contenders have submitted bids to a high-level review committee for prototype development for the Rs 15,000-crore Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft programme. The five prototypes are expected to undertake 1,800 test sorties in a period of seven years to validate the fighter’s flight-control systems.

Article Title: Goregaon East property prices jump 51% and West rates rise 38% as redevelopment, Metro expansion and new road projects transform Mumbai suburb from residential pocket into mixed-use hub
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: Once known primarily as a residential suburb, Goregaon is gradually acquiring a new identity. Better road and Metro connectivity, large-scale redevelopment and the growth of commercial centres are changing the way people live and work here. The suburb is increasingly emerging as a mix of residential neighbourhoods, business districts and retail destinations, say real estate experts.Redevelopment of housing societies has gathered pace in both Goregaon East and West, as a shortage of available land pushes the suburb towards urban renewal. Hundreds of societies, many housed in ageing buildings dating back to the 1960s and 1970s, are opting for redevelopment.Nikhil Bhatia, managing director and co-head of capital markets at CBRE India, said, "Large redevelopment initiatives, including MHADA's Motilal Nagar enclave, are reinforcing Goregaon's transformation."A major connectivity boost is expected from the 12.2-km Goregaon-Mulund Link Road (GMLR), which will connect the Western and Eastern Express Highways through twin tunnels beneath Sanjay Gandhi National Park.The project is expected to cut travel time between Goregaon and Mulund substantially. Another major project, the proposed Versova-Bhayander coastal road, is expected to improve north-south connectivity across the western suburbs, with a planned connector near Mindspace in Malad linking it to GMLR.Metro connectivity is expanding too. Operational Metro Line 2A connects Goregaon with Andheri, Malad, Kandivli and Dahisar. Upcoming Lines 2B and 6 are expected to improve access to BKC, Powai and the eastern suburbs, while extensions of Line 7 towards Mira-Bhayandar and the airport are planned. Together with Goregaon and Ram Mandir railway stations, these links are expected to strengthen the suburb's connectivity with different parts of Mumbai.Improved connectivity is also supporting the growth of commercial activity. Business districts and employment centres such as Mindspace, NESCO, Nirlon Knowledge Park and Film City, along with the Oshiwara Development Corridor, are helping create a mix of offices, homes, shopping and leisure destinations.Developers and property brokers say demand is being supported by connectivity, social infrastructure and proximity to employment centres. Gagan Mehta, director at AGM Vijaylaxmi Group, said, "Goregaon's appeal has widened beyond its traditional catchment areas. We are seeing interest from homebuyers in neighbouring areas such as Jogeshwari, Malad and Kandivali."Residential market data covering projects launched between Q1 2022 and Q3 2026 shows that property prices have risen substantially in both parts of Goregaon.In Goregaon East, the weighted average selling price rose from Rs 26,831 per sq ft of carpet area in 2022 to Rs 40,430 in 2026, an increase of around 51%. In Goregaon West, it went up from Rs 23,926 to Rs 32,944 during the same period, a rise of around 38%.Knight Frank's Gulam Zia said, "Goregaon's property market remained resilient even when east-west connectivity was largely limited to two flyovers and the Metro had only recently opened. Much of the planned infrastructure is still in the pipeline, but demand is likely to grow even without these projects."The two markets have also seen different patterns in new housing supply and sales. Goregaon East recorded 767 apartment launches in 2025, of which 348 had been absorbed. In Goregaon West, 1,323 apartments were launched and 899 were absorbed. In 2026, up to Q3, Goregaon East recorded 241 launches and 35 absorptions, while Goregaon West saw 1,333 launches and 424 absorptions.The figures point to a considerably larger supply pipeline in Goregaon West, where launches have also outpaced sales. In Goregaon East, the gap between launches and absorptions widened in the first nine months of 2026. Absorption refers to cumulative sales from homes launched in the respective year, as recorded in the dataset.Ram Naik, co-founder and CEO of The Guardians Real Estate Advisory, said, "Goregaon's growth is becoming increasingly differentiated across its micro-markets. The east is emerging as a stronger commercial and employment destination, while the west continues to benefit from established residential demand, retail infrastructure and redevelopment."However, the pace of redevelopment and rising population density have also raised concerns. "Construction in Goregaon has gone unchecked. There are serious questions about whether the city's urban environment can absorb further high-density development.Developers wield excessive influence, and there are insufficient checks on the construction of tall buildings," said activist Zoru Bathena.Redevelopment can help replace Goregaon's ageing housing stock, but higher population density can put considerable pressure on drainage, roads, open spaces and public amenities, said activist Anil Galgali. "Rising property prices could also make homeownership increasingly difficult for some buyers." A Mhada official said the scale of transformation requires coordinated planning. "Cluster redevelopment can integrate amenities and infrastructure more effectively than individual projects. "
Article Summary: Goregaon is increasingly emerging as a mix of residential neighbourhoods, business districts and retail destinations. Redevelopment of housing societies has gathered pace in both Goregaon East and West. Developers and property brokers say demand is being supported by connectivity, social infrastructure and proximity to employment centres.

Article Title: Liquor is Noida's problem; in Gurgaon and Delhi, it's obesity
Article Text:
Alcohol consumption also rose from 17.3% to 21.8%, marking the highest spikes among NCR cities (Representative image)

Tobacco use among men aged 15 and above in Noida increased significantly from 29.7% to 38.7%.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





Nearly four in every 10 men aged 15 and above in Noida use tobacco, the highest among four NCR cities, including Delhi, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad, the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) has found.According to NFHS-6 (2023-24), tobacco use among men in Noida increased from 29.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 38.7%, a jump of nine percentage points. Noida also recorded a rise in alcohol consumption from 17.3% to 21.8%, the sharpest increase among the four cities, in the corresponding period.In Ghaziabad, tobacco use among men rose from 22.3% to 28.4% and alcohol consumption from 13.4% to 16.9% during the period.In contrast, Delhi saw a decline in tobacco use among men during the period from 26.2% to 21.3%. Alcohol consumption also went down from 21.6% to 16.1%. Gurgaon also recorded a substantial decline in tobacco use, from 32.6% to 23.7%, although alcohol consumption increased marginally from 18.5% to 19.9%.The survey revealed that the number of women consuming tobacco in Ghaziabad nearly doubled from 1.7% to 3.3% in the three years.The numbers fell in all three other cities - Noida recorded a decline from 3% to 2.3%, Gurgaon from 2.9% to 2.3%, and Delhi from 2.2% to 1.7%.Gurgaon recorded a sharp 17.6 percentage-point jump in overweight and obesity among women. The data show that the number of women in the 15 to 49 years age bracket with a body mass index (BMI) of 25 or above went up from 24.3% to 41.9% during the period. Delhi also recorded a marginal increase, from 41.4% to 42.7%.In contrast, Noida and Ghaziabad recorded declines in overweight and obesity among women. In Noida, the number of women with obesity fell from 34.7% to 30.2%, and in Ghaziabad it came down to 38.7% from 43.7%.However, the decline in overweight and obesity numbers was accompanied by an increase in underweight prevalence among women in all four cities. In Ghaziabad, the proportion of women with a BMI below 18.5 rose from 11.1% to 16%, while Noida recorded a marginal increase from 15% to 16%. Gurgaon also recorded a rise in underweight women, from 9% to 14.1%, while Delhi's figure increased from 10% to 12.4%.A BMI of 18.5-24.9 kg/m² is considered normal or healthy. A BMI below 18.5 is classified as underweight, 25-29.9 as overweight, and 30 or above as obese.The report also revealed contrasting trends in diabetes management across NCR. In Delhi, the number of men aged 15 and above with high or very high random blood sugar levels, or taking medication to control blood sugar, increased sharply from 14.1% to 22.2%. Among women, it rose from 12.2% to 19%.Ghaziabad recorded a sharper incidence among women, from 17.9% to 21.6%, compared with an increase from 20.2% to 20.8% among men. In Gurgaon, the proportion of men with high or very high random blood sugar levels, or taking medication to control blood sugar spikes, rose from 15.4% to 17.2%, while that among women dipped marginally from 13.5% to 13%.Noida was the only city where the high blood sugar indicators declined for both sexes. The prevalence among men fell from 17.2% to 13.6%, while among women it declined from 14.8% to 12.3%.The indicator includes adults with random blood sugar above 140 mg/dl or those taking medication to control it, and does not necessarily represent confirmed diabetes diagnoses.
Article Summary: Tobacco use among men aged 15 and above in Noida increased from 29.7% to 38.7%. Alcohol consumption also rose from 17.3% to 21.8%, marking the highest spikes among NCR cities. Gurgaon recorded a 17.6 percentage-point jump in overweight and obesity among women.

Article Title: Oil prices fall as surplus fears return after a nine-month dry spell in the market
Article Text:
Crude prices fall amid fears of supply surplus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Oil prices fell on Monday as concerns over a potential supply surplus weighed on the market, with shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovering to nearly pre-war levels after months of disruption. The US has also eased restrictions on transporting fuel between its ports, adding to expectations of higher supply.WTI crude futures were trading at $88.35, down 21 cents or 0.24%, while Brent crude futures stood at $95.40, lower by 44 cents or 0.46%.The market is increasingly factoring in the possibility that available supplies could exceed demand in the coming months. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday that the global oil market is expected to move into a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, reversing its earlier forecast of a supply deficit.According to the agency, average oil supply during the quarter could reach 105 million barrels per day, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million barrels per day. The recovery in Middle East exports is expected to outpace growth in global demand, even as attacks on shipping continue."For the first time since the US-Iran conflict began, traders are actively contemplating the possibility of excess supply rather than persistent tightness.That shift in narrative is clearly dampening the tone," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.The IEA also said 71 million barrels from the record release of emergency oil reserves pledged by its members in March would be made available by the end of February. This includes 15 million barrels of diesel intended to ease tightness in the market.The downward movement in prices comes after both major benchmarks had already recorded steep weekly losses. Oil settled lower on Friday as traders assessed signs of reduced geopolitical risks from the US-Israeli war against Iran, now in its ninth month. WTI and Brent had shed 16% and 13%, respectively, over the previous week.Another factor weighing on crude prices is the US decision to extend the suspension of restrictions under the Jones Act for another 90 days.US President Donald Trump extended the waiver, a White House official said on Friday. The law normally requires cargo moved between US ports to be carried by US-flagged vessels. Its suspension allows foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and fuels, including petrol and diesel, between domestic ports, expanding the pool of available tankers.However, the easing of supply concerns does not mean lower shipping costs. Waterer said that elevated freight rates were continuing to support oil prices.The cost of transporting crude remains high because tankers face risks while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Vessel availability has also been affected by ships being tied up in transporting oil through the waterway, where cargoes are transferred to other vessels for onward delivery to refineries.The risks to shipping were highlighted again on Sunday night, when Iran's navy said an oil tanker had caught fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media.
Article Summary: WTI crude futures were trading at $88.35, down 21 cents or 0.24%, while Brent crude futures stood at $95.40, lower by 44 cents or0.46%. The market is increasingly factoring in the possibility that available supplies could exceed demand in the coming months.

Article Title: Indian bonds brace for a rough week as US treasury selloff sends yields soaring

Indian bond selloff to persist after treasuries see worst week in seven months

NEW DELHI: Indian government bonds could face fresh pressure at the start of the week, with rising US Treasury yields and a spike in domestic retail inflation weighing on market sentiment. The sharp selloff in US government debt last week pushed its 10-year yield up nearly 30 basis points, as investors factored in the possibility of a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike.The yield on India's benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond is likely to trade between 7.29% and 7.35% on Monday, a private-bank trader told Reuters. The bond had settled at 7.3079% on Friday.The US 10-year treasury yield closed Friday at around 5.15%, marking a 29-basis-point increase over the week. This was its steepest weekly rise in seven months and came amid growing concerns that the Federal Reserve could announce a larger-than-usual rate hike.The upward movement in US yields followed stronger-than-expected consumer price data for October and hawkish comments from some Federal Reserve members. These developments prompted markets to raise their bets on a bigger rate increase at the Fed's December 9 meeting.Traders are now assigning a 6% probability to a 50-basis-point hike on December 9, according to the CME FedWatch tool.The rise in US yields has also affected domestic bond market sentiment. India's 10-year benchmark yield increased 12 basis points last week, reversing half of the decline recorded during the first week of November."Rising US yields are likely to weigh on sentiment in the local market, especially after the sharp move witnessed in the previous week. Traders will be cautious, and the 10-year bond yield could test fresh highs," the trader said.The domestic inflation numbers have added another concern for the bond market. India's retail inflation accelerated to 6.09% in October, compared with 5.54% in September, crossing the upper tolerance band of the Reserve Bank of India 's inflation target.According to STCI Primary Dealer, the latest inflation reading signals upward risks to food inflation, although fuel prices remain controlled for now.The increase in retail inflation has also strengthened expectations of another interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India in early December.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.

Article Title: In 2016, Priscilla Chan founded a school, 10 years later and after $125 million in donation, Board closed it this year after learning that ...
Article Text:
Funding decision led to the closure of school founded by Priscilla Chan

One of Pricilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg's highest-profile education projects

A ‘whole child’ school

Academic results fell short of expectations

Startup-style approach brought opportunities and challenges

Support package for affected families

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan co-founded a primary school, a tuition-free institution to support low income families via education and healthcare services, has closed after nearly a decade of operations and more than $125 million in funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. The school, launched in 2016 in East Palo Alto, was designed as an ambitious experiment which combined classroom learning with healthcare, family coaching and other support services which focused at helping children overcome the effects of poverty and trauma. However, the school’s board voted unanimously in April 2025 to close the institution after learning that CZI would not continue funding it beyond the 2025-26 academic year, the report added.As per the WSJ report, the board members decided to shut the school after receiving notice that CZI, the philanthropic organisation founded by Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, would no longer finance operations beyond the academic year that ended in 2026. Board president Jean-Claude Brizard told the publication that the school's leadership had explored several options for its future, including a gradual wind-down.He said the board would not have approved the closure without alignment from its largest financial backer.A CZI spokesperson told the newspaper that the decision ultimately rested with the school's board, adding that the organisation's focus was on educational outcomes rather than operating costs.The closure comes as CZI has shifted from social issues toward scientific research. Staff were told early last year that funding for social advocacy had been wound down to match its focus as a science philanthropy and the current legal and policy landscape. CZI said there was no evidence that Zuckerberg and Chan attending President Trump’s inauguration influenced the board’s vote. Brizard called the timing an unfortunate coincidence.The closure marks the end of one of the most prominent education initiatives backed by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. In recent years, CZI has increasingly shifted its focus away from social advocacy and education programmes toward scientific research. The Primary School was created to test a model that integrated education, healthcare and family support under one umbrella. Students received services including dental care, developmental screenings and wellness coaching for parents. The school eventually expanded to two campuses and enrolled nearly 540 children.The private, tuition-free school aimed to support the whole child with services such as free dental checkups, early-intervention screenings and wellness coaching for parents. Chan has said her work as a paediatrician showed her that systems for children are often siloed. About three in four students spoke a language other than English at home. Some elements felt closer to a start-up than a school: teachers signed nondisclosure agreements, and some toddlers wore recording devices at home to measure conversations with caregivers for a language programme. Nearly 540 children were enrolled across two campuses. Chan served as co-founder and board chair for about eight years, until 2023.The Wall Street Journal reported that the school's academic performance struggled to meet both state benchmarks and internal expectations, complicating efforts to replicate the model elsewhere. A Stanford University report cited by the newspaper found that 26% of Primary School students in third grade and above exceeded literacy standards in spring 2025, compared with 14% among local students but 47% statewide. At the same time, supporters of the school pointed to achievements beyond academics. School leaders highlighted improvements in student well-being and access to healthcare services. According to the report, about 85% of students received annual well-child visits, well above the rate for children covered by Medicaid in the county.The report also mentioned that the school chose various unconventional practices. The staff worked closely with community clinics to identify high-needs families, while the parents frequently visited campus for coaching sessions and child-development programmes. But the school also witnessed a lot of hurdles such as turnover among principals and difficulties in establishing long-term systems for special education and student discipline. A former employee of the school also told WSJ that building the school's model required more time and planning than initially anticipated.Former consultant Katherine Carter told the publication that launching a school involved far more support and preparation than many people expected.CZI also pledged $50 million after the closure of the school was announced for an easy transition process. The commitment from CZI included support for local community organisations, payment of remaining school lease and education savings accounts for students.The families also received contributions ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 depending on a child's age and programme level, the report said.The WSJ report further states that some of the parents also said that they expected the school top remain a long-term fixture in the community and were disappointed by its closure. However, some also praised the support services it offered. The school officially closed in June, brought an end to a decade-long experiment which sought to reimagine how the schools could support children both inside and outside the classroom.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan co-founded a primary school in East Palo Alto, California. The tuition-free institution aimed to support low income families via education and healthcare services. Nearly 540 children were enrolled across two campuses. Board voted unanimously in April 2025 to close the institution after learning that CZI would not continue funding it beyond the 2025-26 academic year. School's academic performance struggled to meet state benchmarks and internal expectations.

Article Title: Days after resigning over affair, Jensen Huang ‘talks’ return as Nvidia CEO; ‘Everyone loves Jensen’ call, ‘war room’ and more that could bring him back
Article Text:
Jensen Huang eyes Nvidia comeback

Jensen Huang’s allies are building a ‘war room’ to lobby Nvidia’s board

Elon Musk and over 8,000 Nvidia employees have signed the ‘ Bring Jensen Back ’ letter

Washington and Nvidia’s board structure stand in the way of Huang’s return

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, just four days after he resigned from the company he co-founded and ran for 33 years. The former Nvidia CEO has discussed the possibility of a comeback with close confidantes, according to a Financial Times report citing multiple people familiar with the matter. This comes even as an independent probe ordered by Nvidia’s board continues to look into the conduct that led to his exit.Huang stepped down as president, CEO and director on November 12. His resignation followed reports of extramarital affairs with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who has been accused of spying for China, and with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him. A report of a third relationship, with another Nvidia employee, surfaced hours after he left. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the $4 trillion chipmaker reports its quarterly results on Tuesday.One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to push for the former CEO’s return. The group will also try to win over the White House, and the effort reportedly has Huang’s backing.“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person said.Two large Nvidia shareholders have also left the door open. On Friday, Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker wrote to the board urging it to keep “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang”.Even his allies aren’t sure how to repair his reputation. “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offence,” one person involved in the effort acknowledged to the FT.The public face of the campaign is an open letter urging the board to “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”. By Monday morning India time, it carried 169,588 names, with 8,364 identifying themselves as current Nvidia employees. That is close to 20% of the company’s roughly 42,000-strong workforce.The numbers come with a caveat. The campaign itself says affiliations are self-reported and not verified, and reports have flagged entries such as “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor”.The marquee names are real, though. Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator’s Garry Tan, Shopify’s Tobias Lutke and Replit CEO Amjad Masad are all on the list. Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick wrote that Huang had “erred, yes”, but added, “I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company.”Inside Nvidia, an internal suggestion box post asking the board to weigh employee sentiment has drawn more than 1,600 comments, most of them backing Huang. The campaign is also nudging institutional investors to raise the issue on Tuesday’s earnings call at 5pm ET, which is 3:30am IST on Wednesday.Silicon Valley has seen this play out before. In 2023, OpenAI’s board fired Sam Altman and reinstated him within days after staff and investors revolted.In Washington, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia should look “outside” the company for its next chief. “They need a dramatic shake-up,” he said in a television interview.He also wants Nvidia to explain within 10 days whether it knowingly let its most advanced AI chips reach China. He called that more important than the affair.Huang has limited leverage inside the company as well. Unlike several other founder-CEOs, he does not hold a controlling stake and cannot overrule the board, the FT noted. The board, now chaired by former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones, has reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor, though Nvidia said no “formal” process has begun.The Alice Huang angle got murkier over the weekend. Megaspeed, which bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips, said she left the company “effective Aug. 30, 2025” and currently has no role there.Huang and other Nvidia officials have agreed to testify before Congress, though no date has been set. Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang declined to comment to the FT.In 2023, Huang said he could run Nvidia for another three or four decades. Whether he gets that chance now rests with a board he can’t outvote and a government that wants someone new.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, just four days after he resigned from the company he co-founded and ran for 33 years. His resignation followed reports of extramarital affairs with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who has been accused of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO.

Article Title: Upset shareholders sue Intel; say that company did not share on time the disastrous …

Upset shareholders sue Intel; say that company did not share on time the disastrous …

Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan disappointed by manufacturing supply shortages

Intel says budget laptop chips are already sold out

Intel shareholders have sued the company, accusing it of hiding the impact of a long slowdown in PC sales that led to its stock price falling nearly 29% in a single day, Reuters reports. The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, by shareholders led by a Michigan pension fund. They claim Intel failed to disclose in time how weak PC sales and excess inventory would hurt its revenue. The shareholders also allege that Intel raised $23 billion by selling shares at $95 each in mid-August, even though the company was already halfway through what they called a “disastrous” third quarter.As stated in the Reuters report, the shareholders allege that Intel's problems with PC sales and excess inventory outweighed ⁠data center construction and other benefits related to the artificial intelligence boom.Intel reported its quarterly results on October 30. The California-based company then projected lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue and profit. It also forecasted a prolonged slowdown in PC sales.Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan then told analysts that he was disappointed by manufacturing supply shortages, an "unprecedented memory crunch," and resulting softness in PCs. "We need to ​address these challenges ​with urgency," Tan added.During the earnings call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for the company’s budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips “is outstripping supply.”CFO David Zinsner confirmed that the chips are now sold out. “We've seen significant growth in Wildcat Lake. It’s coming exactly at the right time because it’s cost-optimized and we’re seeing a lot of focus in that regard,” he said.Wildcat Lake chips are appearing in lower-cost Windows laptops, including the new Dell XPS 13 and HP OmniBook 5 14. These devices are positioned as more affordable options in a market where rising memory costs have put pressure on PC prices.However, some of these laptops start with just 8GB of RAM. That could be a limitation for users who need to run several applications or handle demanding tasks, particularly as Windows laptops can struggle with lower memory configurations.
