Article Title: Canada PM Mark Carney sends a message to the US government; says: Canada has best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, and we are is going to move forward either way, if you do
Article Text:
'Canada is going to move forward either way'

China discussions on agenda

Any investment must include manufacturing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Auto sector caught in trade dispute

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that Canada could turn to Chinese and other international automakers if trade negotiations with the United States fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry, delivering a pointed message to the Trump administration amid ongoing trade tensions. According to a report by Associated Press, speaking to reporters in Cambodia, Carney said Canada remains committed to maintaining a North American automotive market but stressed that Ottawa would pursue other opportunities if US trade policies continue to disrupt the sector. “We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Carney said. “That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions.”Carney also revealed that the negotiations with the US President Donald Trump’s administration is still a priority for Canada, but he also warned that the outcome of these talks could influence whether Ottawa seeks deeper partnerships with European, Chinese or Japanese automakers. On being asked that if there’s a possibility of Chinese investment being used as a leverage in talks with Washington, Carney dismissed the suggestion.“It’s not leverage. But action, reaction,” he said.Referring to Canada's workforce and manufacturing assets, Carney added: “If they’re not fully utilized in a North American context, that provides other opportunities. Canada is going to move forward either way.” The remarks amount to one of the clearest signals yet that Canada is preparing alternative strategies should trade talks with the US fail to protect the country's automotive industry.The comments made by Carney came ahead of a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzen later this week. It is expected that the Chinese vehicle manufacturing and investment are said to feature prominently in the discussions. Earlier this year, Canada and China reached to an agreement enabling thousands of Chinese vehicles into Canadian market at reduced tariffs. As part of the deal, Canada’s tariff on Chinese EVs was cut from 100% to 6.1%, with an initial annual import cap of 49,000 vehicles that will gradually increase over time. In return of this, China agreed to reduce the tariffs on agricultural products from Canada. Carney has earlier argued that the agreement between Canada and China could help in attracting Chinese investment and also create jobs on Canada.The Canadian prime minister stressed that any future Chinese investment would need to involve significant manufacturing operations inside Canada rather than simply assembling imported components. “It’s not just about kit cars,” Carney said. “There has to be a manufacturing aspect involved.” He said any investment would need to meet labour standards, establish manufacturing facilities and build domestic supply chains over time, including the use of Canadian critical minerals required for electric vehicle production.The North American auto industry is deeply integrated, with manufacturers including Ford, General Motors and Stellantis operating facilities across Canada, the US and Mexico. Vehicle parts often cross borders several times before final assembly. However, Trump's tariff policies have disrupted that system and intensified pressure on automakers to shift production to the United States.The impact has already been felt in Canada. Ottawa recently threatened legal action against Stellantis after the company moved planned Jeep Compass production from Brampton, Ontario, to Illinois and agreed to sell its idled Canadian assembly plant.Ontario Premier Doug Ford has also criticised Canada's EV agreement with China, warning that increased imports of Chinese-made vehicles could put Canadian jobs at risk and potentially undermine access to the US market.
Article Summary: Carney said Canada remains committed to maintaining a North American automotive market. He stressed that Ottawa would pursue other opportunities if US trade policies continue to disrupt the sector. Comments came ahead of a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. It is expected that the Chinese vehicle manufacturing and investment are said to feature prominently in discussions.

Article Title: UpGrad launches advisory arm 'upGrad Next' to help enterprises navigate AI-led transformation
Article Text:
Focus on workforce transformation in AI era

Combining consulting, skilling and hiring

Veteran consulting leaders join

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Building an Indian-origin advisory institution

Edtech and workforce development company upGrad has launched upGrad Next, a new enterprise advisory practice aimed at helping organisations redesign their operating models and workforces for an AI-driven future. The company said the new division will bring together advisory services, workforce skilling and talent hiring under a single platform, positioning itself as a one-stop solution for enterprises undergoing large-scale organisational transformation.According to upGrad, the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence across businesses has created a growing need for organisations to rethink how work is structured and how employees are prepared for new technology-driven roles. The company said upGrad Next has been established by a team of senior consulting leaders who have left global consulting firms to build what it describes as an outcome-led, Indian-origin advisory institution. Four leaders have joined as Managing Directors, with additional senior partners expected to join in the coming weeks.upGrad noted that while consulting partners have often launched specialist advisory firms in areas such as tax and mergers and acquisitions, this is the first time in decades that a workforce and HR advisory practice in India is being founded by former partners from leading consulting firms.The company said upGrad Next will advise C-suite executives on organisational and structural transformation while leveraging upGrad's existing ecosystem to deliver employee reskilling, leadership development and recruitment services. upGrad said it worked with more than 700 enterprises during FY26 and plans to use that experience to help companies implement workplace changes more effectively.“The last decade was about digital transformation for organisations. The next decade will be about transforming the workforce to manage, and generate returns from, that transformation,” said Ronnie Screwvala, Co-Founder and Chairperson of upGrad.“Advice, the ability to skill talent at scale, and enablement through AI and technology now need to sit under the same roof. That is what upGrad Next is built to do,” he added.The leadership team at upGrad Next includes Anandorup Ghose, Hrishikesh Godbole, Krishna Chaitanya Malladi, and Dinkar Pawan, all of whom bring extensive experience in human capital consulting, organisation design, compensation strategy and workforce transformation. Ghose, who will serve as Managing Director, previously led rewards consulting practices at Deloitte in India and globally. Godbole is a former EY partner with experience spanning consulting and corporate leadership roles at EY, GE and Godrej.Malladi previously worked in Deloitte's human capital consulting practice, advising organisations on workforce productivity and organisation design, while Pawan brings expertise in HR consulting, economics and executive compensation.Commenting on the launch, Anandorup Ghose, Managing Director of upGrad Next, said businesses would increasingly be judged by their ability to unlock workforce potential rather than simply adopt new technologies. “The next decade won't be won by those who adopt technology fastest, but by those who unlock human potential most effectively,” Ghose said.“Our ambition is to build a world-class, Indian-origin institution that stays accountable for outcomes,” he added. The launch marks upGrad's latest expansion beyond higher education and online learning as it looks to strengthen its presence in enterprise consulting, workforce development and AI-led organisational transformation.
Article Summary: UpGrad Next is a new enterprise advisory practice aimed at helping organisations redesign their operating models and workforces for an AI-driven future. The company said upGrad Next has been established by a team of senior consulting leaders who have left global consulting firms to build what it describes as an outcome-led, Indian-origin advisory institution.

Article Title: Lokpal withdrew jt secretary recruitment ad after whistleblower Sanjiv Chaturvedi application: RTI
Article Text:
Sanjeev Chaturvedi

Dehradun:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





Lokpal of India withdrew its recruitment process for the post of joint secretary on Aug 17, citing “administrative reasons”, nearly four months after advertising the vacancy and receiving an application from Uttarakhand cadre Indian Forest Service officer and whistleblower Sanjiv Chaturvedi, an RTI response filed by Dehradun-based activist Bhupendra Chanda has revealed. The RTI reply said that the anti-corruption ombudsman had cancelled the exercise without explaining the decision.Lokpal issued the vacancy circular on April 27, inviting applications for the post. Chaturvedi applied, and Uttarakhand govt forwarded his application on June 13, conveying its no-objection and consent for his deputation. However, Lokpal withdrew the circular on Aug 17, stating that no further action would be taken on applications received under it.The cancellation marked another setback in Chaturvedi’s efforts to secure a deputation to Lokpal, which began in Dec 2019. On Dec 23 that year, Uttarakhand govt forwarded his request to the Union ministry of environment, forest and climate change (MoEF&CC) with its consent. The ministry sought a copy of the vacancy advertisement on Feb 5, 2020, but took no substantive action for nearly two and a half years, prompting Chaturvedi to approach Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT).During the proceedings, CAT asked Centre to show “magnanimity and openness” while considering his request. On Sept 1, 2022, it directed the secretary of MoEF&CC to decide the matter within eight weeks in consultation with the department of personnel and training (DoPT).However, the ministry returned his application through an order dated Oct 3, 2022, signed by a director-rank officer rather than the secretary. It said the request “did not accompany any vacancy circular” and cited DoPT instructions issued on Dec 12, 2013, which stated that applications not submitted against an advertised vacancy “should not be forwarded”. The ministry also referred to section 10 of the Lokpal Act, which empowers the Lokpal chairperson to appoint the institution’s staff.The April 27 circular appeared to address the procedural objection raised in 2022, as Chaturvedi had applied for an advertised vacancy with Uttarakhand govt’s consent. Yet, the exercise was cancelled. The RTI response did not establish whether Chaturvedi’s application influenced the withdrawal decision.Meanwhile, Centre directly appointed another officer as joint secretary in Lokpal in July 2026, without following the vacancy circular route. The appointment order reportedly included a relaxation of the cooling-off period requirement for the officer.
Article Summary: Lokpal of India withdrew its recruitment process for the post of joint secretary on Aug 17. The anti-corruption ombudsman had cancelled the exercise without explaining the decision. Uttarakhand cadre Indian Forest Service officer and whistleblower Sanjiv Chaturvedi applied.

Article Title: Great expectations: A year at Southampton, India’s first foreign university campus
Article Text:
The campus, which operates from an IT park building in Gurgaon, has a corporate feel to its layout but with quirky additions for the student vibe

The UK pull factor

Trade deal boost

The quality question

Easier on the pocket

A value question

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





Diya Aneja had an uncommon subject combination in mind for her undergraduate. As the clock ticked on the admission cycle in 2025, the IB student from Gurgaon was ready to give up one of the troika of economics, business and psychology she was insisting on -- subjects she liked and a pairing that would hopefully AI-proof her in the job market. “I didn’t find a college that gave me the major-minor combination I wanted,” says the 20-year-old, who has just completed her first year of BSc honours in economics at Southampton University Delhi.In Aug 2025, Southampton became the first international university to open a direct, full-fledged campus in India under UGC regulations after the ministry of education in 2023 opened the gates to foreign institutions (Deakin was the first foreign university to open a campus in India in 2024, at GIFT City in Gandhinagar, but comes under special financial zones rules).Diya’s course combines core economics subjects with behavioural economics and management ethics, covering all her interests. It’s one of just six undergraduate courses the India campus of the British university currently offers here, operating out of an IT Park building at Sohna in Gurgaon.The reason Shreya Sethi chose Southampton Delhi for her UG is why a majority of the first batch of students enrolled. Get a UK degree without having to leave India, amid tightening of visa regulations in the West and rising living and airfare costs.Students also see its three-year UG courses, at a time when Delhi University has transitioned to four years, as “an advantage”."My parents thought it'll be too early for me if I left the country after school. They wanted me to finish my graduation before I do that,” says the BSc management student. “Southampton is a leading global university offering me an international degree while letting me study in my own hometown,” says Shreya, for whom the decision was a “no-brainer”.Southampton held 111th position in the latest QS World University Rankings. The closest Indian campuses in the top 200 are IIT-Delhi at 118 (the highest ever for an Indian institute), IIT-Mumbai at 134 and IIT-Madras at 170.Shradhha Surana, a BSc accounting and finance student, says she relates to the university’s pedagogical approach that goes beyond textbooks. “We are growing along with the campus,” she says.The Delhi campus’s UG and masters programmes are all market-facing – software engineering, business management, accounting and finance, computer science, economics, and creative computing in UG, and data science, economics, finance and international management in masters.Among most students on the campus TOI spoke to on completion of their first year, the expectation of access to placements and landing an international job after graduation is strong. In particular, they are looking forward to the option of studying one semester at the main campus in Southampton, available to eligible students in the second year.A first-year student who joined the university from Hyderabad (he did not wish to be named) says, “The best performers will get the opportunity to study at the UK campus for one semester, so that also gives me motivation to do well.”This year, Southampton was joined by University of Liverpool opening its India campus, at Bengaluru. International Chamber of Commerce UK chair Lord Karan Billimoria, who recently led a Chartered Association of Business Schools delegation to India, tells TOI the UK–India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement signed this July will play a big role in more British educational institutions setting up India campuses.“The agreement marks a major milestone in expanding bilateral trade, and education will play an important role in realising its potential,” he says. “The Indian govt is giving a strong signal to international institutions through National Education Policy, and individual states are actively encouraging UK universities and business schools to set up campuses in India.”The UK’s restrictive immigration measures have limited the mobility of international students, so universities there must look globally to keep teaching an international cohort of students, Billimoria admits.Southampton Delhi's academic provost Elloise Phillips says the university is making sure the exact academic standards followed on the UK campus are replicated here — the same curriculum, blackboard modules, assessments and reading list. Those adept in the UK methodology of teaching have been hired as faculty members — about 60% have either studied in the UK or worked there.The staff has undergone extensive induction and training covering Southampton’s teaching, assessment and quality bars. Some faculty members are simultaneously taking the university’s PG certificate in education course, which will give them the same internationally recognised teaching qualification as their peers in the UK.“We also follow the same processes when it comes to marking and moderation of work and external examining. It’s generally the same external examiner as the one who looks at the UK and the Malaysia campus, so they can do cross-comparisons,” Phillips says.The university, according to her, is strict on quality assurance so the Delhi campus has the same credibility as the one in the UK. “We recognise that employers will want clarity, so transparency is important. Students will graduate with a University of Southampton qualification, and their records will clearly reflect the programme they have completed,” she says, adding that the university will continue to build awareness and understanding of the academic model in India.Phillips says what makes Southampton different is that it offers the combination of a UK university education with the opportunities and context of studying in India. “Students have access to an internationally experienced faculty, industry engagement, career support and a curriculum designed to develop both disciplinary knowledge and the skills needed to apply that knowledge in the workplace,” she adds.The undergraduate programme fee at Southampton University Delhi is Rs 13.8 lakh a year. On the UK campus, it is £28,000 for international students, which translates to around Rs 35.7 lakh a year.Where there is a huge difference is the campus and the presence of a diverse peer group. Southampton Delhi occupies two floors of a corporate building at International Tech Park. By that happenstance, the campus has the look of a corporate office with quirky additions to give it a college feel. There are breakout zones with cushions and a personal sitting area where students can work and read, plus a library and snack zones.The India campus accepts CBSE, CISCE and state boards marks as well as IB and Cambridge qualifications. Students can apply with Class XII results or predicted grades. A major requirement negated while applying in Delhi versus the UK is an IELTS qualification.Pointing to campus infrastructure, among other things, education consultant Adarsh Khandelwal says it makes him sceptical about the value for money that foreign universities offer through their India campuses.“It’s not just about getting a foreign degree. It’s also about immersing yourself in the culture,” he says. “And since international campuses in India cannot offer this, he says, the programmes are not becoming as popular as anticipated.”What sets US and UK higher education institutes apart, Khandelwal explains, is the interdisciplinary coursework. “There are at least 30-40 courses at an undergraduate level.” With few degrees on offer here, there is no way to achieve this. When it comes to hiring in India, he adds, a recruiter will give a graduate from an international university campus and a private university the same kind of first job.Aarti Srivastava from National Institute of Educational Planning points out that the world's top universities have still not set up campuses here. “If an Oxford or Harvard does this, their standards will be diluted.That will give rise to another kind of discrimination during job interviews where people will ask whether the degree is from Harvard India or US,” she says.Srivastava feels the quality of research on Indian campuses will invariably be compromised as compared to their foreign counterparts because of bureaucratic hurdles and problems with securing grants.While Southampton understands trust issues, the India campus is hoping the calibre of its first batch of graduates will put doubts to rest. Phillips says the university has a combined strength of 200 students for now, and plans to keep intake small to ensure more individual attention. “We are not in competition with anyone. We are just another option,” Phillips says.(With inputs from Shruti Sonal)
Article Summary: Southampton University Delhi is the first international university to open a direct, full-fledged campus in India under UGC regulations. The campus operates from an IT park building in Gurgaon. The UK–India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement signed this July will play a big role in educational institutions setting up India campuses.

Article Title: Dip in Delhi pollution levels, but Yamuna's condition becomes flashpoint during Chhath
Article Text:
Delhi pollution dips , but Yamuna foam sparks row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





NEW DELHI: Delhi witnessed improvement in pollution levels on Monday, with PM2.5 concentrations dropping significantly across several monitoring stations. However, the overall air quality index (AQI) continued to remain in the ‘poor’ category, while a thick layer of smog lingered over several parts of the national capital.The improvement came despite the absence of significant rainfall or strong winds, raising questions over the sharp decline in pollution levels. Experts said weather conditions were favourable for the dispersion of pollutants, but did not fully explain the scale of the improvement.The AQI stood at 216 at 7.05am on Monday, in the ‘poor’ category, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). Sirifort recorded an AQI of 346 and NSIT Dwarka 330, both in the ‘very poor’ category.Among other areas, Punjabi Bagh recorded an AQI of 276, Chandni Chowk 271, ITO 267, North Campus Delhi University 259, IIT Delhi 258, JNU 240, Burari 221 and Anand Vihar 205. Okhla Phase 2 recorded an AQI of 191, while IMD Lodhi Road registered 149, both in the ‘moderate’ category.The improvement in air quality came as the condition of the Yamuna remained a political flashpoint during Chhath Puja celebrations in the capital.Thousands of Purvanchali devotees gathered at the river's ghats to offer prayers, even as visuals of white foam floating on the water triggered a political exchange between the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the BJP.AAP accused the BJP governments in Delhi and at the Centre of making false claims about cleaning the Yamuna, sharing videos and pictures purportedly showing devotees performing rituals amid the foam. The party said the visuals exposed the government's claims about the river's clean-up.The BJP rejected the allegations and hit back at the previous AAP government, claiming the Yamuna had become more than half clean in two years.The party also said Chhath celebrations, which it alleged had been restricted at the Yamuna ghats during the previous government, were now being held on a grand scale across the city.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta highlighted the scale of this year's celebrations, saying Chhath was being observed across nearly 1,400 ghats in the capital. The exchange once again brought the Yamuna's pollution into focus during the festival.On Sunday, PM2.5 concentrations had dropped sharply across Delhi, with readings at most of the 32 monitoring stations moving into the ‘good’ or ‘satisfactory’ categories by 6pm. At RK Puram and Major Dhyan Chand Stadium, PM2.5 levels fell below 10 micrograms per cubic metre between 2pm and 3pm.At Tikri Kalan, concentrations dropped from 256–193 in the early morning to 9.84–8.74 between 1pm and 3pm.However, the overall AQI did not reflect the same improvement as it is calculated using a 24-hour average, with the highest pollutant sub-index determining the final category.Delhi's AQI, which stood at 350 at 10am on Sunday, improved to 332 by noon and 290 by 4pm. IIT Delhi remained among the worst-affected locations, recording an AQI of 404 by noon before improving to 350 by 4pm.According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the maximum wind speed recorded was 15 kmph at 2.30pm on Sunday. Although scattered rainfall was reported, IMD monitoring stations did not record rainfall between 8.30am and 5.30pm.Sunil Dahiya of Envirocatalyst said weather conditions were favourable for the dispersion of pollutants, but not enough to explain the scale of the decline.Manoj Kumar of the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) said gaseous pollutants such as nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone also contribute to AQI readings, and sustained improvement would depend on reducing emissions.Meanwhile, AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj on Sunday alleged manipulation in the government's AQI data, questioning the readings at monitoring stations in Jahangirpuri and Anand Vihar.He also claimed that water was being continuously sprayed near the Jahangirpuri monitoring station to artificially lower pollution readings.“The pollution levels published in newspapers today expose alleged manipulation in the government's AQI data... The data shows that IIT Delhi has the highest AQI in the city, even though it is a green and clean campus,” he told ANI.“If the AQI is the highest there, imagine what the levels must be in Jahangirpuri and Anand Vihar,” he said.According to IITM's source-apportionment data until 9am on Sunday, biomass burning contributed 37% of Delhi's pollution load, followed by secondary organic aerosols at 22% and vehicular emissions at 17%. Secondary inorganic aerosols accounted for 7%, while waste burning contributed 5%.The CPCB classifies AQI between 0 and 50 as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’ and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: PM2.5 concentrations dropped significantly across several monitoring stations. But overall air quality index (AQI) continued to remain in the 'poor' category. Improvement came despite absence of significant rainfall or strong winds. Experts said weather conditions were favourable for dispersion of pollutants.
